paper: Li, Zhan, Hu, Chakraborty et al. - Divergent urbanization-induced impacts on global surface urban heat island trends since 1980s
history_definition: Trend/rate of impervious-land growth 1985-2020 (continuous growth-rate sensitivity, not a discrete multi-component trajectory)
method: Partial least-squares regression of trend-sensitivity on rural vegetation, precipitation, population
main_claim: Rural vegetation abundance (biome background), not population, is the dominant regulator of urbanization's SUHI-trend sensitivity
overlap_with_our_candidate: Tests how climate/vegetation background MODERATES the urbanization-to-SUHI relationship; close in spirit to C moderating an H-to-R link, but does not set up an explicit S-vs-S+H information-content comparison or twin-city matching
remaining_gap: No explicit S-vs-S+H model comparison; no twin/analogue design; no H_when/H_where/H_how decomposition

paper: Rentschler, Avner, Marconcini, Su, Strano, Vousdoukas, Hallegatte - Global evidence of rapid urban growth in flood zones since 1985
history_definition: Settlement growth trajectory inside vs outside flood-hazard zones, 1985-2015
response: None - growth-into-hazard is the outcome itself, not an independent environmental response
method: Descriptive/trend analysis of settlement-extent change by hazard class and income group
main_claim: Settlements in the highest flood-hazard zones grew 122% (1985-2015), outpacing safe-zone growth, concentrated in lower/middle-income countries
overlap_with_our_candidate: Directly confirms global data-feasibility of the H_where candidate 'urbanization relative to flood-prone space' (prompt Section 7 item 9); but ALSO independently confirms this audit's own circularity warning (risk register item B): the exact quantity used here (built-up in flood zone) is the same quantity the governing prompt flags as unusable as an independent hydrological R
remaining_gap: Does not test flood-zone growth as a predictor of a SEPARATE realized hydrological outcome controlling for present state; purely descriptive, no S/C conditioning

paper: Chen et al. - Increasing global urban exposure to flooding: an analysis of long-term annual dynamics
response: UEF extent itself (not a separate response)
main_claim: UEF grew more than 4x from 1985-2018, concentrated in Asia
overlap_with_our_candidate: Same circularity concern as Rentschler et al.: growth-into-hazard treated as the outcome, not as an independent response
remaining_gap: Same gap as Rentschler et al. above

paper: Rajib et al. - Urbanizing the floodplain: global changes of imperviousness in flood-prone areas
main_claim: Urbanized floodplain area has nearly doubled since 1985, concentrated in hazardous zones
overlap_with_our_candidate: Same circularity concern as the two flood-growth papers above

paper: Jung, Dyson, Alberti - Urban landscape heterogeneity disaggregates the legacy of redlining on land surface temperature
history_definition: Historical redlining grade (1930s HOLC policy label) as a categorical historical-pathway proxy
method: Mixed-effects models + landscape heterogeneity decomposition, controlling for present land cover
main_claim: Redlining's apparent LST effect fragments once present-day landscape heterogeneity (tree canopy etc.) is accounted for
overlap_with_our_candidate: CONCEPTUALLY CLOSEST MATCH FOUND: tests historical pathway (H, categorical) -> LST (R) explicitly after controlling present-day land cover (S) - structurally the same logical test as candidate Test A, with categorical H and 3-city US scope instead of a continuous global multi-decade trajectory
collision_risk: PARTIAL COLLISION - close in logic, distant in scope/operationalization
remaining_gap: No continuous multi-decade developmental trajectory H; no global scope; no twin-city/analogue design; no incremental out-of-sample model-comparison framing

paper: Legacies of redlining lead to unequal cooling effects of urban tree canopy
main_claim: Tree-canopy cooling effect of present vegetation is modulated by historical redlining legacy
overlap_with_our_candidate: Same structural overlap as Jung/Dyson/Alberti: H=historical policy, R=LST, with present canopy as an S-like control
remaining_gap: US-only; categorical H; no global multi-decade trajectory

paper: Not even past: legacy effects of redlining on heat inequities across spatial scales in Philadelphia
main_claim: Legacy effects persist but vary across spatial aggregation scales
overlap_with_our_candidate: Same conceptual family as the other redlining-LST papers, narrower single-city scope; the scale-sensitivity finding is itself directly relevant to this audit's MAUP risk (register item L)
remaining_gap: Single-city; informs MAUP risk rather than colliding with the main question

paper: Zhao et al. - The influence of urban form on surface urban heat island and its planning implications: evidence from 1288 urban clusters in China
history_definition: Urban form (shape irregularity, centrality of built-up pattern) - a present/recent-form proxy, not an explicit multi-decade trajectory
main_claim: Centralized/compact development raises SUHI; shape irregularity lowers it
overlap_with_our_candidate: Large-N (>1000) precedent for form-variable-to-SUHI analysis at sub-global scale; closer to an S-type than an H-type analysis
remaining_gap: National, not global; 'form' here is closer to present-state S than to a historical trajectory H

paper: Enhanced surface urban heat islands due to divergent urban-rural greening trends
main_claim: Divergent urban/rural greening trajectories enhance SUHI over time
overlap_with_our_candidate: Directly relevant to the rural-reference-contamination risk (register item J): shows the rural reference area itself has its own trend/legacy, not just the urban core
remaining_gap: Not framed as H vs S; supporting evidence for an identifiability risk, not a collision on the main question

paper: Surface urban heat island effects intensify more rapidly in lower income countries
history_definition: Development/income trajectory (implicit, not explicit historical urban form)
main_claim: SUHI intensifies faster in lower-income countries
overlap_with_our_candidate: Directly relevant to development-level confounding risk (register item G): shows income trajectory alone predicts SUHI trend, a strong candidate confound for any H effect
remaining_gap: Supports a specific identifiability risk; not a direct test of the candidate question

paper: Surface urban heat island across 419 global big cities
journal: Conference/journal via ResearchGate (venue not independently reconfirmed)
main_claim: Establishes feasibility of large-N global SUHI cross-city comparison
overlap_with_our_candidate: Precedent for large-N global SUHI comparability (supports Section 8/10 feasibility), not a history-effect test

paper: Bastin et al. (authorship not independently reconfirmed) - Understanding climate change from a global analysis of city analogues
history_definition: N/A - matches FUTURE climate of city A to PRESENT climate of city B, not historical-pathway divergence among present-day twins
response: Future climate (not an environmental response to history)
main_claim: Most cities' future climates resemble another city's present climate, often to the south
overlap_with_our_candidate: Methodological precedent for city-twin/analogue matching, relevant to candidate Tests B/C's matching machinery, but answers a different question (future-climate communication, not history-to-response)
remaining_gap: Analogue-matching machinery itself is not novel; novelty of Test B/C rests on matching on (S,C) and testing against historical divergence D_H, which this body of work does not do

paper: Barthel et al. (authorship not independently reconfirmed) - Social-ecological memory in urban gardens: retaining the capacity for management of ecosystem services
main_claim: Social-ecological memory sustains ecosystem-service stewardship in urban gardens
overlap_with_our_candidate: Not a collision on the scientific question, but directly relevant to the terminology audit: shows (social-)ecological memory already has an established, different meaning when applied to urban systems
remaining_gap: N/A - informs the terminology audit, not the main collision question
